programme.title: New Zealand by Train
programme.desc: There are three railway routes in New Zealand.The first, Northern Explorer, stretches across the North Island, from Auckland to Wellington.Coastal Pacific runs from Picton to Christchurch, offering breathtaking views from the east coast of the South Island.The "TranzAlpine" route leads from Christchurch to the wild west coast.The total length of railway lines is 4,000 km.Their construction was extremely demanding and difficult.New Zealand, being a small island country, is characterized by a huge variety of terrain.Here you can find subtropical and rainforests, mountains, oceans, volcanoes and plains with railway tracks running through them.Each episode will discuss the engineering difficulties encountered during the construction of the railway network and present places worth seeing.Local residents talk about the everyday challenges that life in this area poses for them The director of the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy, Peter Jackson, chose New Zealand as the setting for the adventures of the hobbit and his company.It is famous for its picturesque landscapes that are the perfect background for fantastic, out-of-this-world stories.They are extremely diverse - peaceful river valleys and green hills contrast with numerous volcanoes.However, such terrain constitutes a huge challenge for the engineers responsible for the construction of the railway.Viewers will learn about the attractions of the Kiwi country from the perspective of train passengers following three routes - Northern Explorer, Coastal Pacific and TranzAlpine.The Hobbit's Land The journey is divided into two stages.The first one goes through the North Island, where the capital Wellington and Auckland - the country's largest city - are located.There is no shortage of untouched areas that viewers of "The Lord of the Rings" could see.For example, the Ngauruhoe volcano located here played the role of Mount Doom.The Northern Explorer route is 681 km long.It runs via numerous viaducts from Auckland to Wellington.Passengers travel through, among others:farmland, the engineering masterpiece of the Raurimu Spiral and the volcanic plateau.The creators of the documentary combine phenomenal landscapes with a story about the culture and history of the end of the world.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough, who has been bringing viewers the secrets of fauna and flora for almost seven decades, this time takes on the role of a guide to the largest continent on Earth.The film material was shot for almost four years.In seven episodes, documentarians showed from a new perspective the natural riches of Asian mountain ranges, ocean depths, dense jungle and inaccessible caves.They captured a stunning variety of the wildest places - from the frozen land of seals to colorful coral reefs.An ocean teeming with life. The first episode of the series will reveal to viewers the magic of the underwater world.Asia has the longest coastline of all continents and the richest coral reefs on Earth.Its seas are connected by some of the most powerful sea currents in the world.It is home to over sixty percent of all marine species.Specialized cameras recorded, among other things, sharks chasing fish called Moorish idols.In an interview, the filmmakers admitted that this was one of the most difficult sequences to capture.They also visited the remote Seal Islands and the Sea of ​​Japan, where they tracked squid.Finally, they explored the secret world of the Coral Triangle - the richest concentration of marine life on our planet.
